tiers.criteria: 100% of FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass.
80-99% of FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass. Core feature works, minor edge cases missed.
60-79% of FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass. Main flow works but significant gaps.
30-59% of FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass. Partial implementation.
< 30% of FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass, or code doesn't parse.
100% of PASS_TO_PASS tests still pass. Zero regressions.
90-99% of PASS_TO_PASS tests pass. 1-2 minor regressions.
70-89% of PASS_TO_PASS tests pass. Several regressions.
< 70% of PASS_TO_PASS tests pass. Agent broke existing functionality.
Intent-revealing naming that reads like natural language. Consistent formatting matching existing codebase. Docstrings on all public interfaces. Complex logic has inline comments.
Highly readable, consistent formatting, clear naming. Minor gaps in documentation of non-obvious logic.
Mostly readable but some cryptic names (temp, data1, v), or complex algorithms lack inline comments.
Inconsistent naming/casing, large undocumented blocks, confusing layout.
Completely cryptic naming throughout, no comments, messy indentation.

hard_caps.condition: Agent uses single-letter variable names in business logic (not loop counters)

tiers.criteria: Flawless separation of concerns. Single-responsibility functions (mostly < 20 lines). Clean dependency injection. Loose coupling. Zero copy-pasted logic.
Strong modularity, clear layer boundaries, short functions (mostly < 30 lines), mockable dependencies.
Standard structure but some implementation details leak across layers; a few functions are monolithic or contain duplicate logic blocks.
Monolithic functions (> 80 lines), high cyclomatic complexity (> 15), deep nesting (4+), or systemic copy-pasted code.
Extreme debt: gigantic functions (> 150 lines), God Classes, global mutable state, tight coupling.

hard_caps.condition: Any single new file exceeds 500 lines
Business logic placed directly in API route handlers (bypassing service layer)

tiers.criteria: Defensive programming throughout. Specific exceptions handled. Safe resource management. No magic constants. Input validation at boundaries. Concurrent safety where applicable.
Strong defensive coding. Specific exceptions handled. Clean resource lifetimes. Minor magic constants (< 2).
Errors handled but generic catch-all blocks common. Some magic constants. Missing validation on 1-2 edge cases.
Silent error swallowing. Manual resource management with leak risks. Bare except: pass in business logic.
Silently swallowed exceptions in critical paths. No input validation. Hardcoded credentials.

hard_caps.condition: Agent uses bare except: or except Exception: pass in business logic
Errors in payment/settlement/data-mutation paths are silently swallowed

tiers.criteria: Follows all established repo patterns: repository pattern, service layer, Pydantic schemas, consistent naming (snake_case), proper file placement, imports organized per existing style. New code is indistinguishable from existing code.
Follows most patterns. 1-2 minor deviations.
Follows general structure but notable deviations: putting business logic in API layer, or skipping repository pattern.
Partially follows conventions. Mix of patterns used inconsistently.
Ignores repo conventions entirely. Code works but doesn't fit the codebase.

hard_caps.condition: Agent skips the repository pattern entirely (direct DB queries in service or API layer)

tiers.criteria: Changes are minimal and focused. Only touches files necessary for the task. No unnecessary refactoring, no unrelated changes, no dead code introduced.
Mostly minimal. 1-2 minor unnecessary changes.
Some unnecessary changes: touching files that didn't need modification, or adding unused imports/utilities.
Significant unnecessary changes: refactoring unrelated code, adding helper functions never called.
Massive unnecessary changes that obscure the actual feature implementation.

gatekeeper_rules.effect: Overall capped at 20 regardless of other dimensions

score_synthesis.formula: Sum of all 7 dimension scores (max 100). D1+D2 anchor the score while D3-D7 differentiate within the functional tier.

calibration_persona: Grade based on the severity, frequency, and systemic nature of issues. Avoid leniency bias (being too generous or easily impressed by boilerplate scaffolding) AND paranoia (being overly punitive for isolated minor issues). An isolated infraction in an otherwise strong codebase should not drop a dimension score by more than one tier.
